thesis: Partial observation and aggregation can hide causal distinctions or create memory, so useful simplicity depends on the observable and action domain.
role: Extend laboratories to scales, equations and intervention.

ideas.statement: Eliminating variables can require history or latent state; aggregate models must compete on the same observable and fidelity.
Equation discovery depends on coordinates, libraries and observations, while equivalent fits must retain mechanistic ambiguity.
Compression can help experiment search or erase relevant causal differences; control must assess policy-induced distribution changes and safe domain exit.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Observationally identical causal mechanisms require selected interventions whose costs are counted.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Complicated cellular-automaton images do not prove irreducibility, and real-system control needs domain-specific validation.

audit.notes: Complete batch read; headings and navigation excluded from idea ranking.
